01-feature-building.notes: All 18 pass the 5 hidden contract tests and their own suites; I reproduced every RESPONSE.md test count. Separation came from my probe harness and a shared mutation run. The one functional contract break is J (duplicate depends_on entries produce a bogus empty-cycle error). Robustness gaps: A, C and O have recursive cycle finders that raise RecursionError at about 1000+ jobs. H and M reject whitespace-only IDs. P is quadratic. Close calls: B, L and F are within 0.25. B gets full marks for a clean implementation plus a reference-oracle test suite. L has the strongest tests (17/17 mutants) and the most precise SCC diagnostic, but a heavier implementation with heappush-based priority validation. F is cleanest but has no oracle test and lets the FIFO-tie mutant survive. Mutation caveat: suites that assert exact message wording (B, G, H, K, N, Q) show apparent survivals on validation and cycle mutants because those tests fail on my reference too; I discounted those. A 0.25 contract edge went to submissions whose cycle diagnostic names the cycle itself rather than every blocked job; both satisfy 'include the IDs involved'. Not verified: behaviour with one-shot iterator depends_on (contract types it as a tuple).

04-project-maintenance.notes: The main cross-cutting finding: the fixture's flat layout (slugkit.py next to test_slugkit.py) makes setuptools auto-discovery abort with 'Multiple top-level modules discovered'. M and Q reproduced this with a real setuptools and quoted the error. Only A, C, E, G, K, M and Q declare py-modules. In the other 11 submissions, CI's 'pip install -e .' fails on every matrix entry and no release artifact can be built. That cost about 0.5-0.75 in each of compatibility and CI. The second split is the distutils replacement. LooseVersion.__str__ returns the input, so identity (A, D, E, G, K, L, M, N, Q, R) is correct. packaging-based versions (C, I, J with fallback; F, O, P strict) rewrite '1.02', '1.0-rc1', 'v1.0' and 'RC' spellings, and the strict ones raise on input that used to be accepted. B's regex validator rejects 1.0.post1, 1.0.dev3 and local versions. H strips whitespace and 'v'. Close calls: Q and K both 9.75. Q is ranked first because it diagnosed and documented the fixture build failure; K's suite is marginally stronger (in-suite parity test). G and E tie at 8.75. G is ranked ahead because its tests pin more spellings and E copied build tools from an external uv cache, while E has the stronger artifact verification. L and H tie at 6.75: L is ahead because it keeps behavior, H is richer but changes it. B and C tie at 5.5: B is ahead because C used the network, against the brief. Not verifiable here: ruff (not installed; I approximated with an AST unused-import and line-length check, which found nothing beyond missing final newlines in C and N), actual setuptools builds (setuptools unavailable; the py-modules conclusion rests on setuptools' discovery logic plus M's and Q's reported reproductions), and runs on 3.10-3.12. Own suites were re-run on Python 3.14 with packaging (all OK) and 3.13 without packaging (C, F, I, J, O, P error on import, as expected for a declared runtime dependency).

08-social-media.notes: All 18 meet the numeric limits: LinkedIn 124-166 words, Bluesky 215-278 chars, Instagram 79-117 words with at most four hashtags, all Bluesky replies under 300 chars. L's Instagram (79-80 words) and R's RESPONSE.md (151 by wc, about 147 real words) are the only borderline cases. So the field splits mainly on factual discipline. B, E, I, M, N, O and R invent product facts (support emails, menu paths, resumable indexing, language testing, lab invoicing offers, Japanese support), while D, K, J, P and H invent nothing. Among the clean ones, J, P and H lose voice and quality points for stiff, brief-aware hedging ('launch details don't specify', 'no verified training-data policy') that undercuts the brand's clear local-processing fact. I treated a firm 'no' to the training question as acceptable when it is argued from local processing (A, G, K), and as overclaiming when it becomes absolute policy ('never collect, inspect'). A flat 'no lab plan' is a mild extrapolation; routing the question without claiming either way (D, K, F) is best. Closest calls: D vs K, where D's voice and Instagram scene edge it; and A/C/G tied at 9.0, ordered C > A > G for C's more useful outage diagnostic and G's slip inviting payment details into DMs. N vs O are tied on criteria logic but O's outage reply has no apology. 12-frontend-editorial.notes: The top group is close. D (9.25) edges J and M (9.0) on composition and its fully accessible mode/form handling. J has the best single display motif but its invalid-email message is not announced. M has the most substantive reading mode but an understated issue title. Five submissions tie at 8.75 (B, A, P, N, G); they are ranked by visual strength, then interaction. O has arguably the boldest art but loses points for the confirmed first-click submit failure caused by a blur-validation layout shift. Every page passed the no-overflow, no-remote-request checks. All text contrast was computed against solid backgrounds; contrast over SVG/gradient art was not measured. Fonts named in CSS (e.g. Iowan, Didot) are absent on this Linux machine, so all judgements use the fallback rendering shown in the screenshots. Screen-reader output was not tested with real AT; accessibility judgements rest on DOM semantics (labels, aria-live, aria-invalid, aria-pressed), keyboard tab traversal (every focused control had an outline or box-shadow except the E and M email inputs) and computed contrast.

13-frontend-playful.notes: I and L tie at 9.0. I ranks first for its more distinctive 'a little odd' shape language and richer undo paths (per-row plus toast); L is equally complete and adds observation entry. M and D (8.75) are visually the most polished but more serene than odd. M ranks above D because D's hero pushes the desktop queue to about y=600. H and E tie at 5.5; H ranks above E because its undo works, while E's Watered undo is broken. C's underlying work is substantial, but an unclosable modal (display:flex overriding [hidden]) blocks the whole UI for pointer users, so it scores near the bottom; I did not grade it on what would appear if the modal were fixed. Contrast figures are a heuristic computed against the nearest opaque ancestor background, so gradients and images are not modelled. I did not test screen readers.
